ledger.x: 390 BC: 'In 390 BC, the Senoni Gauls invaded Italy from the north and occupied Picenum north of the Esino river' (Picentes page); the Senones page has them 'settling on the Adriatic coast between Ariminum (modern-day Rimini) and Ancona, displacing the Umbrians' in 'the 4th century BC' (it rejects Livy's c.
298-295 BC: the Third Samnite War coalition; 'Rome defeated a coalition of Samnites, Gauls, Etruscans, and Umbrians at Sentinum' (295).
284-283 BC: Lake Vadimon ('284 BC, not 283 BC' per the Boii page; 283 on the Roman-Etruscan Wars page) with the Boii and Etruscans.
283 BC: 'Rome finally subjugated them in 283 BC'; the ager Gallicus Roman (Sena Gallica; Ariminum colony 268).
283 BC: the Cisalpine Senones end; the Senones of Gaul (Agedincum) are a different polity in Caesar's wars (58-52).

wars.name: Gallic sack of Rome
wars.outcome: Rome defeated at the Allia and sacked ('390-387 BC'); no land held

certainty.note: The Adriatic coast between the Marecchia and the Esino.
